SMTO-EXE-0042 — SMTO won't repeat a step that already failed twice

GUID: e31781bc-8b46-491a-8313-fc9718ba82bd
Slug: unchanged-operation-rejected
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • The same action has already failed twice, and nothing has changed since. SMTO didn't try it a third time, so nothing new was run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the earlier failed steps in the task and read their error messages. They explain what went wrong, which is what needs to change.
  2. Fix that cause if you can, for example switch on the Gateway computer, correct a file name, or give the needed access. Once something real has changed, SMTO allows the action again.
  3. Tell SMTO in the conversation what you changed, or suggest a different way to do it, then ask it to continue. New information lets SMTO try again or choose another approach instead of repeating the same failure.

What success looks like

  • SMTO runs the action again, or a different one, and the step completes.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the conversation name, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't just resend the same request; SMTO will refuse it until something changes.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The execution.retry_bound check found at least two equivalent prior failures at the same evidence revision, with no qualifying fresh-read exception, and refused another unchanged attempt without executing it.

What this means

  • The retry guard found at least two equivalent prior failures at the same evidence revision, without a qualifying fresh-read exception, and refused another unchanged attempt. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • The retry guard found at least two equivalent prior failures at the same evidence revision, without a qualifying fresh-read exception, and refused another unchanged attempt.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the retained failure count, operation signature and evidence revision; identify the actual cause or observation needed to change the decision.

How to fix it

  • Read the prior failures for the same call fingerprint (agent_runtime.native.operations.execute_operation) and fix their specific cause, or change the arguments or approach. A new observation that advances the run's evidence revision, or a different call, allows another attempt.
  • Inspect the prior failure and current target state. Correct its specific cause or choose a different supported action before repeating it.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A meaningful prerequisite or evidence change justifies a new action under the existing retry guard.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
